findings.evidence: Both `LinearEquiv.ofInjective` arguments in the diff have the identical five-line injectivity block.
findings.fix: State one lemma for arbitrary submodules `P ≤ X₀`, `Q ≤ Y₀`, `P' ≤ X₁`, `Q' ≤ Y₁` saying this map is injective, and use it in both equivalences.
findings.issue: The proof that `(WithLp.linearEquiv 2 𝕜 _).symm ∘ₗ (mapIncl _ _).prodMap (mapIncl _ _)` is injective (`.symm.injective.comp <| by rw [LinearMap.coe_prodMap]; exact .prodMap (Module.Flat.tensorProduct_mapIncl_injective_of_right _ _) ...`) is copied verbatim into both `kerExternalProductBlockEquiv` and `kerAdjointExternalProductBlockEquiv`. This is a reusable fact hidden inside two definitions.

findings.evidence: The two private range lemmas in the diff are line-for-line identical apart from `externalProductBlock_apply_eq_zero_iff` vs `adjoint_externalProductBlock_apply_eq_zero_iff`.
findings.fix: Factor out a generic lemma: the range of `toLp ∘ prodMap (mapIncl P Q) (mapIncl P' Q')` is `{w | w.fst ∈ range (mapIncl P Q) ∧ w.snd ∈ range (mapIncl P' Q')}`. Each kernel lemma then becomes a one-line combination of it with `ker_rTensor_inf_ker_lTensor` and the matching `_apply_eq_zero_iff`.
findings.issue: `range_toLp_prodMap_mapIncl_ker` and `range_toLp_prodMap_mapIncl_ker_adjoint` repeat the same eight-step `rw` chain (`LinearMap.range_comp, LinearMap.range_prodMap, Submodule.mem_map_equiv, LinearEquiv.symm_symm, Submodule.mem_prod`) and the same `simp only [..., LinearMap.ker_rTensor_inf_ker_lTensor]`. They differ only in which `_apply_eq_zero_iff` lemma they use, so a Mathlib rename breaks both.

summary: Proofs are readable and the main kernel argument is commented. The injectivity of the Künneth inclusion and the range-equals-kernel rewriting are each written out twice instead of being factored into shared lemmas.
